role: Consumed-Dev mechanism replication; eligibility for a larger Dev qualification, not a generalization, SOTA, or leaderboard claim.
scientific_question: Does the adaptive executable installer preserve terminal Official success while reducing repeated strong-Agent repair across projects, or was the ceph pilot a one-sample parameterization accident?
selection_rule: Include every remaining project with a pre-existing Official-successful envsolve_pro_m1 state-v0001 seed after excluding ceph, which was consumed by the feasibility pilot. No project is selected from a new-method outcome.
condition_rationale: Supported Python-version changes are ordinary deployment requirements and are observable before execution. Returning to D0 tests whether the D1 updater retains earlier compatibility. The sequence is fixed without observing replication outcomes.

arms.static: Replay the latest saved executable program; after current public failure, invoke a fresh gpt-5.6-sol xhigh Agent with the previous program and current feedback, qualify on the current condition, and save the latest success without historical replay.
arms.adaptive: Use the identical replay-first and Agent fallback path, expose prior verified conditions to the updater, and retain a candidate only after current qualification plus fresh replay on every prior verified condition. The only learned object is the executable program.

controlled_equalities: same project-specific D0 seed within each pair
same gpt-5.6-sol model and xhigh reasoning effort
same Spark arm64 execution host without GPU exposure
same repository revision, image, public verifier, shell tools, target-condition input, source-cache policy, and postepisode Official evaluator
same fallback trigger and ability to replace the full program
unique_treatment_difference: Adaptive receives the list of prior verified deployment conditions and must pass their fresh replays before retaining P_{t+1}; static retains the latest current-condition success.

execution_policy.within_project: Follow each project's fixed D1 and D2 arm order. Complete both D1 arms before either D2 arm.
execution_policy.between_projects: Projects may run concurrently for throughput. Concurrency, network failures, and censored runs must be recorded; do not reorder within a project based on intermediate outcomes.
execution_policy.retry: Retry only infrastructure-censored or invalid engineering runs from the same unchanged input state. Retain all invalid-run costs and reasons.
execution_policy.official_feedback: EnvBench Official is postepisode only and is never returned to an Agent or used to alter a later arm.

primary_outcomes: D1 and D2 Official success for each arm
whether D2 required a new Agent fallback
secondary_outcomes: input, cached-input, output, and reasoning tokens
full lifecycle, preflight, qualification, regression, and Official wall time
download bytes and retained storage when available

decision_rule.promote_to_larger_dev_qualification: Adaptive has no fewer D2 Official passes than static, has no unexplained historical or Official regression, and avoids a D2 Agent fallback required by static on at least two of three projects after all lifecycle costs are charged.
decision_rule.retain_without_promotion: Adaptive preserves Official success and shows a fallback advantage on only one project, or infrastructure censoring leaves fewer than three valid pairs.
decision_rule.kill_current_form: Adaptive loses terminal Official success, cannot retain prior verified conditions, or has no D2 fallback advantage on all three projects while adding historical replay cost.

excluded: ceph, whose sequential outcome is already observed
protected Canary or Official Test data
cross-project memory or natural-language trajectory memory
cache, image, checkpoint, RL, or harness-self-modification treatments
new hashes, frozen contracts, or gates
